paragraphs.text: וַיִּפְשַׁ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֥וֹת אַחְאָֽב׃

i18n.en: And Moab rebelled against Yisra'el after the death of Ach'av.

notes.official: Moab's revolt after Ach'av's death is narrated in 2 Kgs 3:4-27 and from the Moabite side on the Mesha Stele (c. 840 BCE), which names Omri and 'his son'. The verse repeats almost verbatim at 3:5.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּפֹּ֨ל אֲחַזְיָ֜ה בְּעַ֣ד הַשְּׂבָכָ֗ה בַּעֲלִיָּת֛וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּשֹׁמְר֖וֹן וַיָּ֑חַל וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ לְכ֣וּ דִרְשׁ֗וּ בְּבַ֤עַל זְבוּב֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י עֶקְר֔וֹן אִם־אֶחְיֶ֖ה מֵחֳלִ֥י זֶֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And Achazyahu fell through the lattice in his upper chamber that was in Shomron, and he became ill. And he sent messengers and said to them, "Go, inquire of Ba'al-Zevuv, the elohim of Eqron, whether I shall recover from this sickness."

notes.official:
*baʿal zəḇûḇ ʾĕlōhê ʿeqrôn* 'Ba'al-Zevuv, the elohim of Eqron' (ASV 'Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron'). The MT name means 'Lord of the fly/flies' (LXX *Baal muian theon*). Many scholars see in it a deliberate deformation of *baʿal zəḇûl* 'Baal the Prince', a Ugaritic epithet (*zbl bʿl*) and the source of New Testament *Beelzeboul* (Mark 3:22) (Cogan and Tadmor, *II Kings*, AB 11, 1988; Day 2000). The MT form is kept (`baal-zevuv-elohei-eqron-2-kings-1`; `mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). Lower-case 'elohim' for a non-YHWH referent (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`).

Names: Achazyahu = Ahaziah (MT short form *ʾăḥazyâ* here, long form at 1:18, normalized per `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`); Shomron = Samaria; Eqron = Ekron. *diršû* 'inquire of' (`darash-yhwh-seeking-oracle`) is the technical verb for consulting an oracle. *malʾāḵîm* 'messengers' are human envoys (`malakh-yhwh-messenger`).

paragraphs.text: וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה דִּבֶּר֙ אֶל־אֵלִיָּ֣ה הַתִּשְׁבִּ֔י ק֣וּם עֲלֵ֔ה לִקְרַ֖את מַלְאֲכֵ֣י מֶֽלֶךְ־שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם הַֽמִבְּלִ֤י אֵין־אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתֶּם֙ הֹֽלְכִ֔ים לִדְרֹ֕שׁ בְּבַ֥עַל זְב֖וּב אֱלֹהֵ֥י עֶקְרֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: But the messenger of YHWH said to Eliyahu the Tishbite, "Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Shomron, and say to them, 'Is it because there is no Elohim in Yisra'el that you are going to inquire of Ba'al-Zevuv, the elohim of Eqron?'

notes.official: *ûmalʾaḵ YHWH* 'But the messenger of YHWH' (`malakh-yhwh-messenger`; ASV 'the angel of Jehovah'): one messenger answers the king's messengers, the same noun in both. *hămibbəlî ʾên-ʾĕlōhîm bəyiśrāʾēl* 'Is it because there is no Elohim in Yisra'el...?': the refrain of the chapter (vv 3, 6, 16), with anarthrous capital 'Elohim' set against the lower-case 'elohim of Eqron' (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`). The prophet's name is in the short form *ʾēliyyâ* here and in vv 4, 8, 12, normalized to Eliyahu (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וְלָכֵן֙ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַמִּטָּ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־עָלִ֥יתָ שָּׁ֛ם לֹֽא־תֵרֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה כִּ֣י מ֣וֹת תָּמ֑וּת וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ אֵלִיָּֽה׃

i18n.en: Now therefore thus says YHWH: 'You shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.'" And Eliyahu went.

notes.official: *hammiṭṭâ ʾăšer-ʿālîṯā šām lōʾ-ṯēreḏ* 'You shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up': the oracle plays on 'go up' / 'come down' (*ʿlh* / *yrd*), which run through the chapter (vv 6, 9-11, 15-16) and on into 2 Kgs 2.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּשׁ֥וּבוּ הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים אֵלָ֑יו וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מַה־זֶּ֥ה שַׁבְתֶּֽם׃

i18n.en: And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, "Why is it that you have returned?"

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו אִ֣ישׁ ׀ עָלָ֣ה לִקְרָאתֵ֗נוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֵינוּ֮ לְכ֣וּ שׁוּבוּ֮ אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֣ח אֶתְכֶם֒ וְדִבַּרְתֶּ֣ם אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַֽמִבְּלִ֤י אֵין־אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתָּ֣ה שֹׁלֵ֔חַ לִדְרֹ֕שׁ בְּבַ֥עַל זְב֖וּב אֱלֹהֵ֣י עֶקְר֑וֹן לָ֠כֵן הַמִּטָּ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־עָלִ֥יתָ שָּׁ֛ם לֹֽא־תֵרֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה כִּֽי־מ֥וֹת תָּמֽוּת׃

i18n.en: And they said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go, return to the king who sent you, and say to him, "Thus says YHWH: Is it because there is no Elohim in Yisra'el that you are sending to inquire of Ba'al-Zevuv, the elohim of Eqron? Therefore you shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die."'"

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם מֶ֚ה מִשְׁפַּ֣ט הָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלָ֖ה לִקְרַאתְכֶ֑ם וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: And he said to them, "What was the manner of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו אִ֚ישׁ בַּ֣עַל שֵׂעָ֔ר וְאֵז֥וֹר ע֖וֹר אָז֣וּר בְּמָתְנָ֑יו וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אֵלִיָּ֥ה הַתִּשְׁבִּ֖י הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: And they said to him, "A hairy man, with a belt of leather girded about his loins." And he said, "It is Eliyahu the Tishbite."

notes.official: *ʾîš baʿal śēʿār* 'A hairy man', literally 'a man, possessor of hair' (ASV). It may describe the man himself or his clothing: NRSV 'A man with a garment of hair', cf. the prophet's *ʾadderet śēʿār* 'hairy mantle' (Zech 13:4) and John the Baptist's camel-hair garment (Mark 1:6). The ASV is kept, and the clothing reading is noted here. *ʾēzôr ʿôr* 'a belt of leather' (Mark 1:6 again). The Tishbite = from Tishbe (see 1 Kgs 17:1).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלָ֛יו שַׂר־חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו וַיַּ֣עַל אֵלָ֗יו וְהִנֵּה֙ יֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֔ר וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו אִ֚ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דִּבֶּ֖ר רֵֽדָה׃

i18n.en: Then he sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him, and behold, he was sitting on the top of the hill. And he said to him, "Man of the Elohim, the king has said, 'Come down.'"

notes.official: *śar-ḥămiššîm wāḥămiššāyw* 'a captain of fifty with his fifty': a military unit (Ex 18:21; 1 Sam 8:12). *ʾîš hāʾĕlōhîm* 'Man of the Elohim', the articular title, rendered following the Hebrew (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`). Eliyahu sits on 'the top of the hill' and the captain orders him to 'come down', continuing the up/down motif of v 4.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲנֶ֣ה אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ וַיְדַבֵּר֮ אֶל־שַׂ֣ר הַחֲמִשִּׁים֒ וְאִם־אִ֤ישׁ אֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֔נִי תֵּ֤רֶד אֵשׁ֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְתֹאכַ֥ל אֹתְךָ֖ וְאֶת־חֲמִשֶּׁ֑יךָ וַתֵּ֤רֶד אֵשׁ֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַתֹּ֥אכַל אֹת֖וֹ וְאֶת־חֲמִשָּֽׁיו׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu answered and said to the captain of fifty, "If I am a man of Elohim, let fire come down from the skies and consume you and your fifty." And fire came down from the skies and consumed him and his fifty.

notes.official:
*ʾim-ʾîš ʾĕlōhîm ʾānî* 'If I am a man of Elohim': anarthrous in Eliyahu's reply, against the captain's articular address (v 9). The Hebrew alternates, and the translation follows it (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`). The wordplay *ʾîš* 'man' / *ʾēš* 'fire' drives the scene (Cogan and Tadmor, *II Kings*).

*tērēḏ ʾēš min-haššāmayim* 'let fire come down from the skies': here the noun is bare *ʾēš*, not *ʾēš ʾĕlōhîm* (cf. v 12). *šāmayim* per the central `shamayim` ('skies'). The fire descends where the king demanded that the man 'come down' (v 9).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֜שָׁב וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלָ֛יו שַׂר־חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַחֵ֖ר וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו וַיַּ֙עַן֙ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו אִ֚ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים כֹּֽה־אָמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מְהֵרָ֥ה רֵֽדָה׃

i18n.en: And again he sent to him another captain of fifty with his fifty. And he answered and said to him, "Man of the Elohim, thus says the king: 'Come down quickly.'"

notes.official: *mahērâ rēḏâ* 'Come down quickly': the second captain makes the summons more peremptory. Articular title as in v 9 (`ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עַן אֵלִיָּה֮ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶם֒ אִם־אִ֤ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֔נִי תֵּ֤רֶד אֵשׁ֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְתֹאכַ֥ל אֹתְךָ֖ וְאֶת־חֲמִשֶּׁ֑יךָ וַתֵּ֤רֶד אֵשׁ־אֱלֹהִים֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַתֹּ֥אכַל אֹת֖וֹ וְאֶת־חֲמִשָּֽׁיו׃

i18n.en: And Eliyahu answered and said to them, "If I am a man of the Elohim, let fire come down from the skies and consume you and your fifty." And fire of Elohim came down from the skies and consumed him and his fifty.

notes.official:
*wattērēḏ ʾēš-ʾĕlōhîm min-haššāmayim* 'And fire of Elohim came down from the skies': the one Kings occurrence of the construct *ʾēš ʾĕlōhîm*, governed by the central `esh-elohim` (anarthrous, as in Job 1:16). The verb is *yrd* 'came down', not Job's *npl* 'fell', and is rendered as written. The central diff for this wave scopes `esh-elohim` to the construct accordingly. The narrator's 'fire of Elohim' answers Eliyahu's 'man of the Elohim' in the same verse (articular this time; `ish-ha-elohim-man-of-the-elohim-prophetic-title-kings`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) cites this verse as proof of the protection the Elohim gave Eliyahu. The line renders the Hebrew construct literally.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּשְׁלַ֛ח שַׂר־חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שְׁלִשִׁ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֑יו וַיַּ֡עַל וַיָּבֹא֩ שַׂר־הַחֲמִשִּׁ֨ים הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֜י וַיִּכְרַ֥ע עַל־בִּרְכָּ֣יו ׀ לְנֶ֣גֶד אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ וַיִּתְחַנֵּ֤ן אֵלָיו֙ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו אִ֚ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים תִּֽיקַר־נָ֣א נַפְשִׁ֗י וְנֶ֨פֶשׁ עֲבָדֶ֥יךָֽ אֵ֛לֶּה חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And again he sent the captain of a third fifty with his fifty. And the third captain of fifty went up, and came and knelt on his knees before Eliyahu, and pleaded with him and said to him, "Man of the Elohim, please let my life and the life of these fifty, your servants, be precious in your sight.

notes.official:
*śar-ḥămiššîm šəlišîm* 'the captain of a third fifty': the MT has the plural *šəlišîm* where an ordinal (*šəlîšî*, used later in the verse) would be expected. It is either a scribal slip or 'a third (set of) fifty'. The ASV construal is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

*tîqar-nāʾ napšî wənep̄eš ʿăḇāḏeyḵā* 'please let my life and the life of ... your servants be precious': *nepeš* as 'life' (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`). The third captain *kneels* (*wayyiḵraʿ ʿal-birkāyw*) and pleads. The two officers before him gave orders.

paragraphs.text: הִ֠נֵּה יָ֤רְדָה אֵשׁ֙ מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַ֠תֹּאכַל אֶת־שְׁנֵ֞י שָׂרֵ֧י הַחֲמִשִּׁ֛ים הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְאֶת־חֲמִשֵּׁיהֶ֑ם וְעַתָּ֕ה תִּיקַ֥ר נַפְשִׁ֖י בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Behold, fire came down from the skies and consumed the two former captains of fifty with their fifties; but now let my life be precious in your sight."

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֞ר מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ אֶל־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ רֵ֣ד אוֹת֔וֹ אַל־תִּירָ֖א מִפָּנָ֑יו וַיָּ֛קָם וַיֵּ֥רֶד אוֹת֖וֹ אֶל־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And the messenger of YHWH said to Eliyahu, "Go down with him; do not fear him." And he arose and went down with him to the king.

notes.official:
*malʾaḵ YHWH* 'the messenger of YHWH' (`malakh-yhwh-messenger`) and *ʾal-tîrāʾ mippānāyw* 'do not fear him' (`al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula`). Eliyahu finally 'goes down' (*wayyēreḏ*), on the divine word and not at the king's command.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('the angel of Yahweh said unto Elijah: Go down with him'). The translation keeps 'messenger' per the central glossary.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר אֵלָ֜יו כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה יַ֜עַן אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֣חְתָּ מַלְאָכִים֮ לִדְרֹשׁ֮ בְּבַ֣עַל זְבוּב֮ אֱלֹהֵ֣י עֶקְרוֹן֒ הַֽמִבְּלִ֤י אֵין־אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִדְרֹ֖שׁ בִּדְבָר֑וֹ לָ֠כֵן הַמִּטָּ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־עָלִ֥יתָ שָּׁ֛ם לֹֽא־תֵרֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נָּה כִּֽי־מ֥וֹת תָּמֽוּת׃

i18n.en: And he said to him, "Thus says YHWH: 'Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Ba'al-Zevuv, the elohim of Eqron — is it because there is no Elohim in Yisra'el to inquire of his word? — therefore you shall not come down from the bed to which you have gone up, but you shall surely die.'"

notes.official: The oracle of vv 3-4 is repeated to the king's face. The refrain adds *lidrōš biḏḇārô* 'to inquire of his word' (`darash-yhwh-seeking-oracle`). 'Elohim' vs 'elohim of Eqron' as in v 3 (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`; `baal-zevuv-elohei-eqron-2-kings-1`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֜מָת כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֣ה ׀ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ וַיִּמְלֹ֤ךְ יְהוֹרָם֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו (פ) בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֔יִם לִיהוֹרָ֥ם בֶּן־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה כִּ֛י לֹֽא־הָ֥יָה ל֖וֹ בֵּֽן׃

i18n.en: So he died according to the word of YHWH which Eliyahu had spoken. And Yehoram reigned in his place, in the second year of Yehoram the son of Yehoshafat, king of Yehudah, because he had no son.

notes.official: The Leningrad Codex has a *pisqa* (paragraph break, פ) in mid-verse after *wayyimlōḵ yəhôrām taḥtāyw* 'and Yehoram reigned in his place' (`piska-b-emtza-pasuq-masoretic-paragraph-break`). 'In the second year of Yehoram the son of Yehoshafat' conflicts with 2 Kgs 3:1, which dates the northern Yehoram's accession to Yehoshafat's eighteenth year. The usual explanation is a co-regency of the Judahite Yehoram with his father (Thiele, *The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings*, 1983; Cogan and Tadmor). The LXX (Lucianic) has a different chronology. Yehoram = Jehoram (two kings of the name, of Yisra'el and of Yehudah); Yehoshafat = Jehoshaphat.

paragraphs.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אֲחַזְיָ֖הוּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֽוֹא־הֵ֣מָּה כְתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Now the rest of the acts of Achazyahu which he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Yisra'el?

notes.official: Achazyahu here in the long form *ʾăḥazyāhû* (cf. v 2). The 'book of the chronicles of the kings of Yisra'el' is the regnal source cited throughout Kings, not the canonical Chronicles. The LXX adds a regnal summary here.
